subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: How do I make a movement better before I make it heavier or faster?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of technique before load: sequencing a progression in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe joint range, control, and mobility work using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply core and postural control in real movement in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving progressive loading with bodyweight or available equipment; correct it and explain why.
Connect recognizing technique breakdown and stopping the set with programming strength and mobility into a wider plan and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a technique-first strength and mobility progression, document the criteria for advancing each movement, and show a completed progression with the criteria met.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Every movement has a seated, supported, reduced-range, and unloaded version. Advancement criteria are set by control and range, never by load lifted relative to any other person.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
